subject: Hosted API pricing follow-up: monthly token volume + peak TPS
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing follow-up: monthly token volume + peak TPS

Hi Susan —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can get you a tailored hosted API pricing scenario. I captured the items we discussed and a few clarifying questions below.

Recap (as we understood it):
- Primary use: customer support automation + fraud-detection assist in agent workflows (generation + retrieval).
- Expected steady-state monthly token volume: ~50M tokens (you noted 30M–80M as a plausible range).
- Peak traffic: roughly 15–20 requests/sec, average ~10 requests/sec; typical prompt + completion ~200 tokens per request => peak ~3,000–4,000 tokens/sec. Please confirm whether you want us to size for tokens/sec or requests/sec.
- Target procurement timeline: Q4 2026 (PO in ~6–8 weeks after price confirmation).
- Sensitive data: PII in prompts; SOC2 + encryption-at-rest required.

Action items / Questions:
1) Confirm the monthly token range (you said 30M–80M) — please pick a best estimate for budgeting.
2) Confirm peak metric preference: tokens/sec (TPS) or requests/sec. We sized above using tokens; if you prefer requests/sec we can convert.
3) Any internal budget target for cost per 1M tokens (ballpark) so we can prioritize model variants in the quote (open-model vs higher-quality model). You mentioned you were aiming for a target near $12/1M tokens but to confirm.

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi to run a quick feasibility check on latency vs cost for the two model classes you care about (open Llama-style vs higher-quality causal model).
- I’ll prepare 2 pricing scenarios (conservative / scaled) showing per-1M-unit economics, monthly totals at 30M / 50M / 80M tokens, and recommended fallback model for peak periods.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up with procurement + engineering next week to confirm SSO/KMS requirements and procurement steps.

I attached the mutual action plan we discussed and a short requirements doc — I can update both once you confirm the numbers above.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: FinPay_ML_requirements.pdf, FinPay_mutual_action_plan.xlsx

From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@finpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finpay.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing follow-up: monthly token volume + peak TPS

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers from our side:
- Best estimate monthly tokens for Year 1: 50M (range 30M–80M).
- Peak preference: we think in requests/sec internally, but since each request is fairly consistent (~200 tokens), you can size off tokens/sec. For procurement I'd like to see both representations.
- Budget: procurement asked us to target ~ $10–$15 per 1M tokens as a stretch; if you can get us to ~$12/1M tokens with SLA and SOC2 that would be ideal.
- Timeline: procurement wants vendor pricing + minimal contract terms by 9/15 so they can include in Q4 planning.

Could you include (in the pricing scenarios):
- Unit economics at $/1M tokens, monthly totals at 30M/50M/80M, and an example at 150M (growth scenario).
- Peak sizing recommendations (hosted shared vs dedicated/dedicated-burst) with rough monthly cost delta.
- Any startup credits or initial discount options for committed volumes (we may be open to a 6–12 month minimum).

We can do the follow-up call on Thursday morning PT. I’ll loop in our procurement contact (procurement@finpay.com) separately for contract details.

Best,
Susan Lee
Head of AI | FinPay
susan.lee@finpay.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing follow-up: monthly token volume + peak TPS

Hi Susan —

Great, thanks for confirming. Below is a first-pass pricing / unit-economics summary and a recommended next step for the Thursday call. Rishi and I will add the latency/throughput notes after our quick sizing check.

Assumptions used here:
- Baseline model (open-ish): target price $8/1M tokens (suitable for many retrieval-augmented generation cases).
- Higher-quality model (latency & quality focused): target price $20/1M tokens.
- Your stated target: $12/1M tokens (procurement stretch target).

Unit economics examples (price per 1M tokens):
- $8/1M => per-token = $0.000008
- $12/1M => per-token = $0.000012
- $20/1M => per-token = $0.00002

Monthly cost examples (rounded):
- 30M tokens: $240 @ $8/1M | $360 @ $12/1M | $600 @ $20/1M
- 50M tokens: $400 @ $8/1M | $600 @ $12/1M | $1,000 @ $20/1M
- 80M tokens: $640 @ $8/1M | $960 @ $12/1M | $1,600 @ $20/1M
- Growth example 150M tokens: $1,200 @ $8/1M | $1,800 @ $12/1M | $3,000 @ $20/1M

Peak sizing note (quick):
- You mentioned ~200 tokens/request and 15–20 reqs/sec peak => ~3k–4k tokens/sec peak. For keys:
  - Shared hosted tier typically handles this profile without dedicated capacity for short bursts, but sustained 4k tokens/sec across long windows (minutes+) will push cost and may need dedicated capacity for predictable latency.
  - For sustained peak over multiple minutes, estimate dedicated baseline pricing to be ~25–40% higher in fixed monthly commit but with much better latency predictability and lower per-token variable cost at scale (we'll model both).

Next steps for Thursday:
- I’ll bring detailed numbers for 30/50/80/150M at three price points and a recommendation for hosted shared vs dedicated sizing.
- Rishi will validate target peak TPS assumptions and call out any model-specific throughput limits we should be aware of.
- If you confirm $12/1M as your procurement target, I’ll include a committed 6-month option with a step-down tier for months >75M.

I attached the updated MAP and requirements doc for your procurement team to review.

Would 10:00 AM PT on Thursday work for the 30-min sync?

Thanks —
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing follow-up: monthly token volume + peak TPS

Quick internal note before the Thursday call —

On the traffic sizing: the customer’s profile (200 tokens/request, 15–20 reqs/sec peak => ~3k–4k tokens/sec) is fine for shared hosted for short bursts. My recommendations:
- We should prepare two technical scenarios in the Thursday deck:
  1) Hosted shared tier (no commit) — cheaper upfront, slightly less predictable p99 latency under sustained bursts.
  2) Dedicated baseline with burst capacity — recommended if FinPay expects sustained peaks beyond ~2 minutes; it gives consistent p50/p90/p99 and predictable unit economics.
- Latency estimate (rough) for the higher-quality model: p50 ~120–180ms per token on our hosted runtime; end-to-end request latency will depend on prompt length but plan for ~1–2s for a 200-token completion. We’ll validate with a quick perf run for the exact model variant.

Actionables for Thursday:
- Ben: put the pricing table + committed 6-month step-down option in the deck.
- Marissa: please include any accelerator/discount guidance we can offer for enterprise procurement.
- Rishi: will run perf test today and report real p50/p90 numbers for the chosen model (I'll share results in the deck).

-rishi
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
